newsitem.title: USA: Colombians convicted in drug case with Cuba tie.
newsitem.headline: Colombians convicted in drug case with Cuba tie.

text.p: Two Colombian citizens have been convicted on U.S. cocaine smuggling charges, a conviction aided by Cuban officials' rare decision to provide testimony in the case, U.S. officials said on Thursday.

Francisco Williams-May and Arcadio Wilson, the captain and chief engineer of the freighter Limerick, were arrested on Oct. 1 by U.S. Coast Guard officers who boarded the ship after it began to sink in international waters off Cuba's coast near the U.S. Naval Base at Guantanamo Bay.

The ship, heading from Colombia to the Bahamas, then drifted into Cuban waters, where Cuban officials boarded it and said they found about 6 tonnes of cocaine, which was to have been smuggled into the United States for distribution.

The bales of cocaine were flown to Miami after the United States and Cuba agreed to cooperate, and the detained men were brought to Miami from Guantanamo. A federal jury convicted them on two narcotics-trafficking counts on Wednesday, U.S. Attorney William Keefer said.

A Cuban intelligence officer and three border guards appeared in U.S. District Court in Miami this month to testify in their trial. Law enforcement officials said such cooperation between the two governments, which are avowed enemies, was unusual but not unprecedented.
